newsitem.title: USA: SkyMall sees weak Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: SkyMall sees weak Q2 results.

text.p: SkyMall Inc said Tuesday it expects to report second-quarter net income of between $0.03 a share and $0.04 a share due to lower gross margins.

Analysts had expected the company would earn $0.11 a share for its second quarter, according to First Call. The in-flight catalog company, which went public last October, said it earned $0.11 a share in the comparable year-ago quarter.
The company said it expects net merchandise sales for the quarter will be about $8.6 million, compared $6.6 million in the year-ago quarter.
Placement fees for the quarter are expected at about $3.5 million compared to $2.7 million a year-ago.

The company said about one-third of the increase in net merchandise sales was attributable to the addition of Southwest Airlines, which was not a participant in the SkyMall program during the second quarter of 1996.
SkyMall attributed the lower earnings to a decrease in gross margin percentage and said its problems will continues for the rest of the year.

"Overall gross margin percentages in the second quarter of 1997 were lower than in the second quarter of 1996 because a significant portion of net merchandise sales in the second quarter of 1997 were derived from our larger participating merchants, who have financial arrangements with the company in which the company retains a lower percentage of sales than with other merchants," said Chairman and Chief Executive Bob Worsley.

"Improving our financial arrangements with merchants is taking longer than anticipated, and we expect the issues affecting gross margin percentages in the second quarter to continue until the end of 1997," he said.

The company said it is confident it can improve gross margin percentages. Profitability was also hurt by higher than expected operating expenses to build up the company which will continue for the rest of the year.
